result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks with significant obstructions, including a large flatbed truck parked across the walkway. The street lacks marked crossings and features numerous driveway conflict points from a row of garages, creating a fragmented and potentially hazardous experience for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large red flatbed truck is parked directly on the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground right, blocking the paved walkway area.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: A continuous row of garage doors creates multiple conflict points where vehicles may cross the sidewalk without clear sightlines.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs are visible despite the residential/commercial mix.

interventions.title: Parking Enforcement and Physical Barriers
interventions.description: Implement stricter parking enforcement and install bollards or high curbs to prevent large vehicles from obstructing the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment is primarily industrial with poor pedestrian infrastructure, featuring a narrow roadway with cracked pavement and no lane markings. A large flatbed truck obstructs the left side of the street, and while a sidewalk exists on the right, it lacks a protective buffer from the roadway.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A large flatbed truck is parked on the left side, completely blocking the pedestrian path and forcing anyone walking there into the roadway.

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Surface
hazards.description: Significant longitudinal and transverse cracking in the asphalt creates trip hazards and uneven surfaces.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Separation
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right has no vertical or horizontal buffer from the travel lane, increasing risk from industrial vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion and Buffering
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on both sides of the street with a planting strip or bollards to separate pedestrians from heavy vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway to eliminate cracks and provide a smooth, predictable surface for all users.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Signage
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to define the roadway, along with signage to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians in this industrial zone.
